definitions.explanation: To cause something to move through the air.
To pass over without reading or doing.

examples.japanese: {難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}を飛ばす。
{車|くるま}を飛ばして{来|き}た。
examples.english: I drove fast to get here.

notes:
{飛|と}ばす has three main meanings: causing something to fly, skipping over something, or moving at high speed.

TRANSITIVITY:
- Type: {他動詞|たどうし} (transitive)
- Pair: {飛|と}ぶ (intransitive, to fly)

ASPECT (ている):
{飛|と}ばしている indicates an ongoing action: currently flying something, currently skipping, or currently speeding.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {紙|かみ}ヒコーキを{飛|と}ばす: to fly a paper airplane
- ページを{飛|と}ばす: to skip pages
- {噂|うわさ}を{飛|と}ばす: to spread rumors
- {車|くるま}を{飛|と}ばす: to drive fast
- {冗談|じょうだん}を{飛|と}ばす: to crack jokes

NOTE:
The "skip" meaning is very common in academic and work contexts: {難|むずか}しい{問題|もんだい}を{飛|と}ばす (skip difficult questions).
